title: Sifted homotopy colimits under the associative-algebra forgetful functor
statement:
Use the infinity-category, smallness and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and the model-category, biclosed monoidal product and nonsymmetric monoid-axiom definitions of [lem-coef-associative-algebra-model-transfer]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial biclosed monoidal model category with cofibrant tensor unit and that monoid axiom, equipped with the transferred model structure on its strict associative unital algebras from that node. Suppose moreover that $\mathcal M$ is left proper (pushout of a weak equivalence along a cofibration is a weak equivalence) and tractable (there is a set of generating cofibrations between cofibrant objects). Write $W$ for its weak equivalences and $\widehat W$ for the algebra morphisms whose underlying maps lie in $W$. The forgetful functor induces
$$U_\infty:\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal M)[\widehat W^{-1}]_\infty\longrightarrow\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty.$$
For every small ordinary category $I$ whose ordinary nerve $N(I)$ is sifted, $U_\infty$ preserves $N(I)$-indexed colimits. Here sifted means that colimits in spaces indexed by $N(I)$ commute with finite products. In particular $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is sifted and $U_\infty$ preserves geometric realizations, namely colimits of coherent simplicial diagrams, where $\Delta$ is the category of nonempty finite ordered sets and order-preserving maps.

source.place: Definition 3.18 and Lemma 3.19; Higher Topos Theory Lemma 5.5.8.4 for the geometric-realization indexing shape. The nonsymmetric monoid axiom is used with arbitrary auxiliary objects as in Muro Definition 9.1.

external.place: Muro Definition 9.1, printed p. 1591; Section 10, pp. 1595-1597 (matrix graphs).

proof.text: Fix a small $I$ with sifted nerve. By [lem-coef-sifted-nerve-index-calculus] its finite diagonals are ordinary final. Biclosedness makes tensor preserve colimits in each variable, so for an algebra diagram $B$, the ordinary colimit $L=\operatorname{colim}_I UB$ has multiplication through $L\odot L\cong\operatorname{colim}_I(UB_i\odot UB_i)$ and unit through $\mathbf1\cong\operatorname{colim}_I\mathbf1$. The algebra identities follow from the identities of $B_i$ using the comparison for three factors for associativity and for one and zero factors for the unit laws. A map from $L$ respects these operations exactly when every component from $UB_i$ does. Thus these operations exhibit $L$ as $U\operatorname{colim}_I B$, with the original colimit cocone.

source.place: 5.5.8.6; explicit ordinary associative algebra colimit construction

proof.text: The transferred algebra model structure is combinatorial by [lem-coef-associative-algebra-model-transfer]. Apply [lem-coef-small-diagram-model-rectification] to that model category: every coherent $N(I)$-diagram of localized algebras is equivalent to a strict algebra diagram. Replace it projectively by $A$. By [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison], the localized cocone to $\operatorname{colim}_I A$ is its coherent colimit. As $U$ preserves all weak equivalences by the definition of the transferred structure, $U^IA$ still represents the underlying coherent diagram. It suffices to show that $U^IA$ is good in the precise sense of [lem-coef-sifted-good-diagram-calculus]: its ordinary colimit is also its homotopy colimit. No assertion that $U^I$ preserves projective cofibrant objects is made or needed.

source.place: Lemma 4.1.8.13, first three paragraphs of proof, printed p. 499; compare Propositions 1.3.4.24-25

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-associative-algebra-diagram-cell-filtration] to express $A$ as a retract of $A_\alpha$ built from the constant initial algebra by free cells $T^I(f_\beta)$ with $f_\beta$ projective cofibrations between projectively cofibrant diagrams. We prove by transfinite induction that $U^IA_\beta$ is good and every map $U^IA_\gamma\to U^IA_\beta$ for $\gamma\leq\beta$ is good. At $\beta=0$, the underlying diagram is the constant tensor unit, which is cofibrant by hypothesis and good by [lem-coef-sifted-good-diagram-calculus]; its identity is a good map. At a successor stage put $Y=U^IA_\beta$ and $j:0\to Y$. The initial diagram and its colimit are initial and hence cofibrant, and its homotopy-colimit comparison is an identity after choosing the initial projectively cofibrant replacement. Thus it is good, and $j$ is good by the inductive goodness of $Y$. The free-cell map $f_\beta$ is good by the projective-cofibration clause of the same calculus.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, cellular presentation (a)-(d) and base of induction, printed pp. 500-501

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-associative-word-filtration] to $\mathcal C=\mathcal M^I$ with the pointwise tensor and unit. It is cocomplete with small Hom sets, and pointwise tensoring with $X$ on either side has a right adjoint, $Z\mapsto\bigl(j\mapsto\int_{i\in I}\prod_{\operatorname{Hom}_I(j,i)}[X(i),Z(i)]\bigr)$ with $[X(i),-]$ the corresponding right adjoint in $\mathcal M$, by the Yoneda lemma for ends; strict algebras in $\mathcal M^I$ are exactly $\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal M)^I$, with $U^I$ the forgetful functor. For the successor cell $A_{\beta+1}=A_\beta\amalg_{T^IP}T^IQ$ with $f_\beta:P\to Q$ and $j:0\to U^IA_\beta$, that node expresses $U^IA_\beta\to U^IA_{\beta+1}$ as the sequential composite of pushouts of $j\square f_\beta\square j\square\cdots\square f_\beta\square j$, with $n$ factors $f_\beta$ at word length $n\geq1$. Every such map is good by repeated pushout-product closure in [lem-coef-sifted-good-diagram-calculus]. Its pushout from the preceding good filtration stage is good by that calculus, and its sequential colimit is good by continuous-chain closure. Thus $U^IA_\beta\to U^IA_{\beta+1}$ is good. Composing with earlier good maps uses the finite-chain case of the same closure. At a nonzero limit ordinal $\lambda$, the chain $(A_\beta)_{\beta<\lambda}$ is filtered and $U$ creates filtered colimits by [lem-coef-associative-word-filtration], so $U^IA_\lambda=\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\lambda}U^IA_\beta$; continuous-chain closure again proves goodness and goodness of all stage maps. This completes the induction, including $\alpha$. Finally $U^IA$ is a retract of $U^IA_\alpha$ by [lem-coef-associative-algebra-diagram-cell-filtration], so retract closure proves it good.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, transfinite induction and final word filtration, printed p. 501; nonsymmetric filtration also Haugseng Theorem 3.10

proof.text: Let $Q(U^IA)\to U^IA$ be a projectively cofibrant replacement in $\mathcal M^I$. Goodness proved above says that $\operatorname{colim}_I Q(U^IA)\to\operatorname{colim}_I U^IA$ is a weak equivalence. The former vertex with its cocone is the underlying coherent colimit by [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison]. Step 1 identifies the latter vertex with $U\operatorname{colim}_I A$, and identifies the comparison of cocones with the cocone obtained by applying $U_\infty$ to the algebra colimit of Step 2. Hence that cocone has the same coherent universal property. The diagram equivalences from Step 2 show this for the original coherent diagram, proving preservation of every asserted $N(I)$-indexed colimit.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, derived comparison map at the beginning, printed p. 499

proof.text: By [lem-coef-sifted-nerve-index-calculus], $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is sifted. Substitute $I=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ in the result just proved. Its coherent colimits are precisely geometric realizations by definition, proving the final clause.

theorem associativeAlgebraSiftedLocalization
    {M : Type u} [Category.{v} M] [ModelCategory M]
    [HasLimits M] [HasColimits M] [MonoidalCategory M]
    (_hM : CombinatorialModelCategory.{u, v, v} M)
    (_leftAdj : ∀ X : M, ((tensoringLeft M).obj X).IsLeftAdjoint)
    (_rightAdj : ∀ X : M, ((tensoringRight M).obj X).IsLeftAdjoint)
    (_unit : IsCofibrant (𝟙_ M))
    (_pushoutProduct : ∀ (f g : Arrow M), Cofibration f.hom → Cofibration g.hom →
      Cofibration ((MonoidalCategory.Arrow.pushoutProduct.obj f).obj g).hom ∧
      (WeakEquivalence f.hom ∨ WeakEquivalence g.hom →
        WeakEquivalence ((MonoidalCategory.Arrow.pushoutProduct.obj f).obj g).hom))
    (_monoidAxiom : NonsymmetricMonoidAxiom M)
    (W : AssociativeWordFiltration.Construction M)
    (_transfer : AssociativeAlgebraTransfer W)
    (_leftProper :
      (weakEquivalences M).IsStableUnderCobaseChangeAgainst (cofibrations M))
    (_tractable : ∃ (J : Type v) (j : J → Arrow M),
      (MorphismProperty.ofHoms (fun s ↦ (j s).hom)).rlp = trivialFibrations M ∧
        ∀ s : J, IsCofibrant (j s).left ∧ IsCofibrant (j s).right)
    (A C : SSet.{max u v t})
    (qA : FiniteReedy.largeNerve.{max u v, v, max u v t} (Mon M) ⟶ A)
    (qM : FiniteReedy.largeNerve.{u, v, max u v t} M ⟶ C)
    (_hqA : FiniteReedy.IsLocalization.{max u v, v, max u v t}
      ((weakEquivalences M).inverseImage (Mon.forget M)) qA)
    (_hqM : FiniteReedy.IsLocalization.{u, v, max u v t} (weakEquivalences M) qM) :
    ∃ U : A ⟶ C,
      AreNaturallyEquivalent (qA ≫ U)
        (frameLargeNerveMap.{max u v, v, max u v t, u, v} (Mon.forget M) ≫ qM) ∧
      (∀ (I : Type v) [SmallCategory I], IsInfinitySifted (nerve I) →
        ∀ (F : FiniteReedy.largeNerve.{v, v, max u v t} I ⟶ A)
          (c : (coconeCategory F) _⦋0⦌),
          IsColimiting F c → IsColimiting (F ≫ U) (Spaces.mappedCocone U F c)) ∧
      IsInfinitySifted (nerve SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) ∧
      (∀ (F : SSet.uliftFunctor.{max u v t}.obj (nerve SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) ⟶ A)
        (c : (coconeCategory F) _⦋0⦌),
        IsColimiting F c → IsColimiting (F ≫ U) (Spaces.mappedCocone U F c))
